question.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}>1\}.
$$

The boundary of $A$ is given by

$$
∂A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\bbox[5px,border:1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}\,\}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14245698/assets/c2b4e3d11f16920ce24a279289808d3f5dc4e68563525f1417c8767a5446b461.png)

From the diagram, the boundary points of $A$ lie on the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1.$

Therefore, 

$$
∂A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1\,\}.
$$
